read_scope.notes: Read the complete frozen 22-page PDF, including references and Appendices A–G. Visually inspected every page, all five figures and all twelve tables. Re-rendered Table 9 at higher resolution to resolve an apparent spacing issue; its values are legible and no table defect is asserted. Consulted frozen paper.tex, specificity_results.tex and specificity_component_supplement.tex to resolve notation, wording and layout. Independently verified the PDF SHA256. The extracted abstract contains 152 words after joining line-break hyphenation. No other reviews, earlier versions, progress records or external scientific-validity checks were consulted.

score_reasons.expression: Excellent, precise English with consistent distinctions among a shared response, painter contrasts, aligned response and total mismatch. Section 4.1 uses direct procedural sentences and concrete examples before the equations. Sections 5.3–5.5 explain numerical outcomes in fluent prose and qualify retrospective results economically. Only localized repetition, especially in the discussion and adjacent abstract sentences, remains worth tightening.
score_reasons.structure: The main text makes a coherent question–design–measurement–result–interpretation progression. Primary adjusted comparisons appear first in Section 5.1; pair analysis, calibration and source sensitivity are visibly marked as additional or retrospective. Table 4 brings the two ordering changes together effectively. Appendices preserve estimator derivations, complete comparisons and earlier cohorts without making them prerequisites for following the main study. Remaining improvements are local emphasis and compression rather than reorganization.
score_reasons.new_reader_understanding: The abstract is standalone and within the word limit; it identifies the arms, sample size, reference target, key findings and perceptual limit. Section 3.2 and Figure 1 make the intervention concrete. Table 1 explains feature families and units, while the Monet–Sisley lightness example and the 1/0/1 idealized-error example give useful intuition. The theoretical no-distinction predictor is explicitly distinguished from the observed generic-painting arm. Figures 2–3 and Tables 2–5 have unusually useful interpretive captions. A plain-language interpretation of H at its first definition would make the normalization even easier to retain.
score_reasons.engagement: The question has a clear consequence: a visible name response or a low error need not mean faithful painter distinctions. Figure 1 rewards direct comparison across controls and names, Figure 2 makes labeled mismatch inspectable, and Figure 3 exposes uneven pair responses without hype. The GPT Image 2/FLUX calibration reversal and Nano Banana 2/FLUX scene-averaging reversal give the results a discernible narrative. The discussion briefly repeats the scene-averaging lesson instead of using all of its limited space to sharpen the final reading rule.

strengths: Section 4.1, page 5, explains centering in three plain-language steps and then anchors it in measured Monet–Sisley lightness gaps before introducing notation.

Section 5.1, pages 6–7, directly distinguishes positive alignment from low total error: GPT Image 2 has beta near one yet D = 1.226, while FLUX has the smallest D estimate without an established advantage over the no-distinction benchmark.
Figure 1, page 4, presents the complete six-condition comparison for every model with an explicit fixed selection rule and a clear warning that historical compositions are not matched inputs.

Figure 3, page 8, prints the pair scores inside the heatmaps and labels both zero alignment and reference strength, allowing the reader to see the Monet–Sisley finding rather than merely accept a summary.

Table 4 and its accompanying text, page 9, explain why calibration and averaging across scenes change model order while stating that neither creates improved images or establishes artistic appropriateness.
Section 5.5 and Table 5, pages 9–10, retain the source-sensitive statistical result and explicitly separate retrospective correction from confirmatory evidence.

findings.issue: H is called the reference scale and defined algebraically, but its plain-language meaning as the total squared size of the reference painter differences is left implicit.
findings.reader_effect: A reader new to vector comparisons can follow the supplied 0/1 benchmarks yet still have to reconstruct why this particular denominator is the shared yardstick for both scores.
findings.suggested_change: Replace the scale sentence with a formulation such as: “The total squared size of the reference painter differences, H = sum_a ||r_a||^2, normalizes both scores.” Preserve the equation and shorten the following notation gloss if needed to keep the same footprint.

findings.issue: The opening discussion paragraph says both that averaging scenes can cancel scene-specific differences and, shortly afterward, that averaging first and scoring each scene reward different agreement.
findings.reader_effect: This local repetition slows the concluding interpretation after Section 5.4 has already illustrated the distinction numerically.
findings.suggested_change: Delete the final repeated sentence, or replace it within the same word count with a direct reading rule: “Report whether error scores each scene or the average contrast.” Keep the recommendation to report overall and pairwise alignment alongside original and calibrated error.

findings.issue: Two consecutive sentences introduce “Retrospective checks” and “Separate retrospective calibration,” making the compact abstract slightly repetitive at its final turn.
findings.reader_effect: The status distinction is clear, but the repeated setup uses scarce abstract words before the calibration finding.
findings.suggested_change: Combine the two retrospective findings while preserving their scope, for example: “Retrospective checks find weak Monet–Sisley alignment in five models; calibration rescales each model’s measured differences using other scenes, leaves images unchanged and gives GPT Image 2 the lowest held-out error estimate.” Keep the final perceptual-fidelity sentence and remain below 155 words.

summary: Excellent communication of a bounded digital-reference comparison. The main study can be understood without consulting the repository or technical appendices, and primary results are distinguished from retrospective explanation. The few remaining recommendations concern local wording and emphasis; no consequential claim-fidelity issue was identified within the fixed editorial scope.
